description: The column (or columns) that uniquely identifies a row. Indexed automatically.
`REFERENCES other(id)`: the database guarantees the referenced row exists. Postgres does not index it for you.
Keeps every row of the left table; columns from the right table are `NULL` when there is no match.
`GROUP BY` collapses rows into groups for aggregates; `HAVING` filters the groups after aggregation.
A sorted structure (usually a B-tree) that turns full table scans into fast lookups, at the cost of slower writes.
Runs a query and prints the plan and the real timings, showing whether indexes are used.
